description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training set, comprising 13 distinct slices, each labeled with a dataset name, color-coded, and annotated with its precise percentage contribution. The largest segment is NQ, occupying 31.3% of the dataset and rendered in blue, followed by FEVER at 16.1% in teal, SNLI at 15.4% in orange, and MULTINLI at 11.3% in red. VITAMINC accounts for 13.0% (light teal), not 8.0% as incorrectly stated in the caption, and XSUMHUL contributes 1.6% (light blue). Smaller segments include SCITAIL (1.2%, green), PUBHEALTH (0.5%, dark green), MULTIFIC (0.5%, gray), SCIFACT (0.1%, yellow), ENTFA (1.8%, olive), FACTCC (2.6%, dark orange), and ANLI (4.6%, brown). The chart uses a clean layout with percentage labels directly adjacent to each slice via leader lines, and no slices are exploded or emphasized visually. The segments are arranged in roughly descending order clockwise from the top-right, providing a clear visual hierarchy of data source proportions. The caption’s claim of VITAMINC declining to 8.0% is inaccurate based on the chart, which shows it at 13.0%, and similarly misstates SCIFACT and PUBHEALTH as 0.7% and 0.5% respectively, while the chart shows SCIFACT at 0.1% and PUBHEALTH at 0.5%.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training set, comprising 13 slices. Each slice represents a specific data source with distinct labels, colors, and percentage values. The largest data source is NQ, accounting for approximately 31.3% of the dataset, followed by FEVER at 16.1%. SNLI and MULTINLI are the next largest contributors, with 15.4% and 11.3%, respectively. Notably, VITAMINC shows a steady decline in its contribution compared to previous years, now accounting for only 8.0% of the dataset. Additionally, SCIFACT and PUBHEALTH are among the smallest contributors, with SCIFACT slightly exceeding PUBHEALTH at 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each data source in the training set.
